title: Singular affirmative olla
summary: Match minä, sinä, and hän with the present-tense forms olen, olet, and on.
objectives: Form minä olen, sinä olet, and hän on.
Use the three forms in short complete sentences.
Keep the subject and verb in the same person.

sections.title: Olla links a subject and information
paragraphs: Olla means “to be”. In the present tense, its form changes according to the subject.
Use minä olen, sinä olet, and hän on. The ending tells you who the sentence is about.

sections.title: Build one complete idea
paragraphs: Place the subject first, the matching olla form next, and a supplied location or state last.
The location or state stays unchanged in these exercises, so your only new decision is the olla form.
keyPoints: do not change the supplied context

commonMistakes: Do not use one olla form for every subject.
Do not add a separate word for English “am”, “are”, or “is”.
Keep hän explicit while you are learning the agreement pattern.

practiceExercises.instruction: Write the complete sentence in Finnish.
practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Write “He or she is on time.” Use the explicit subject hän.
practiceExercises.explanation: Hän takes on, the matching present-tense form of olla.
